source.title: AI Daily Digest — 2026-11-12
source.body:
# AI Daily Digest — November 12, 2026

**Top story: the most important person in AI may be about to lose his job, and it has nothing to do with AI.** The **Wall Street Journal** reported late on **November 11** that **Nvidia's board is preparing to oust co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang**, after a *New York Times* report of a second extramarital relationship — this one with an Nvidia executive — layered onto the earlier reporting that tied Huang to a Megaspeed executive whom US intelligence agencies describe as passing information to Beijing. **Reuters** reported the board met late Wednesday to decide; **as of this writing no decision has been announced**. Nvidia fell roughly **8–9% after hours** to about $159, is down around **20% since the scandals began**, and reports earnings on **November 17**. Meanwhile the actual technical news of the window came almost entirely from one lab: **Google DeepMind shipped AlphaGenome 2** (cell-type-specific DNA variant effects) and **Gemini Robotics 2.5** with an open robot-jailbreak benchmark, and Google opened a **Gemini Decisions API** that bills nothing for output tokens. **Alibaba** quietly opened a **two-week, cloud-only Qwen4-Max preview**.

**A note on this edition's sourcing.** This session's network policy blocked **arxiv.org, techcrunch.com, news.ycombinator.com, deepmind.google, siliconangle.com, theneuron.ai** and the other newsletter and tracker domains tried, so the Discovery Pass front-page scans were run through web search rather than by reading those front pages — a weaker instrument for same-day items. Two primary sources **were** reachable and were read directly: **anthropic.com/news**, and **github.com**, where the daily and weekly trending pages (all-languages, Python, TypeScript, Rust) and every repository page in the open-source section below were read. **No DeepMind primary source was reachable**, so the AlphaGenome 2 and Gemini Robotics 2.5 figures below are **DeepMind's own numbers as relayed by secondary coverage** and are labelled as such. The arXiv batch was read via a GitHub-hosted listing, not arxiv.org, so abstracts were not read.

## Notable Papers & Research

### AlphaGenome 2: variant effects in a named cell type, not a tissue average

**Google DeepMind** released **AlphaGenome 2** on **November 11** — the successor to the AlphaGenome model published in *Nature* in January 2026. The shift is conditioning: instead of predicting regulatory effects averaged over a tissue, each prediction is conditioned on a **selected tissue, cell type or cell state**, including conditions a researcher generates from their own single-cell experiment. It was trained on **more than 100 million individual cell profiles across 68 tissues** of bulk and single-cell human and mouse data, and its readouts now add **DNA methylation** alongside gene expression, histone modifications and chromatin accessibility.

On the **TenK10K** immune-cell dataset DeepMind reports it identifying **30% of causal variants** against **16%** for the original model fine-tuned on single-cell data and other specialised tools, and getting the **direction of effect** right in **43%** of cases against **23%**. Access is **non-commercial research via the AlphaGenome API**, with commercial research in **private preview** and AlphaGenome 2 Skills announced for Google Antigravity ([Unite.AI](https://www.unite.ai/google-deepminds-alphagenome-2-predicts-cell-state-variant-effects/), [Interesting Engineering](https://interestingengineering.com/ai-robotics/deepmind-alphagenome-2-causal-dna-variants), [MLQ](`` https://mlq.ai/news/google-deepmind-releases-alphagenome-2-to-predict-how-dna-changes-affect-specific-cell-types-and-disease/ ``)).

*Caveats worth more than the benchmark.* Every condition requires its **own forward pass**, making the model materially more expensive to run than a fixed-track multitask model. Coverage reports that **DeepMind's own paper** cautions that even at high precision the model recovers **only a minority** of the expression-linked and disease-associated variants that statistical fine-mapping nominates as likely causal, and that it is **unclear whether it predicts responses to knockouts, overexpression or dynamic state transitions**. DeepMind states the model is **research-use only, not validated or approved for clinical or diagnostic use**. The paper itself and DeepMind's blog post were **not reachable from this session**; the author list could not be confirmed and is therefore not asserted here.

### The November 11 arXiv batch: agents stop trusting their own memory

The **2611.14xxx** submissions, read via the [ai-radar listing](https://github.com/HuggerHustle/ai-radar/issues/213) (arxiv.org was unreachable, so titles, IDs and authors come from that listing and abstracts were not read). The theme across the agent track is **memory scepticism** — three separate groups attacking the assumption that an agent's accumulated memory is an asset:

- **[Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14320)** (2611.14320) — Yukyeong Lee, Yumin Choi, Jinheon Baek et al. The title states the finding: memory makes agents fail, and linking entries to evidence reduces it.
- **[When Should Agents Remember? Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution for LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14326)** (2611.14326) — Runxuan Tang, Haoyu Gao, Yuyan Ding et al. Stores a lesson only if it survives a falsification check.
- **[ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14492)** (2611.14492) — Kaiyuan Hou, Yang Ping Kuo, Indranil Bhattacharya et al. Compiles SOP-following agents into workflows with **no per-step LLM planning call** — the cost argument against agentic scaffolding, made constructively.

On the training-theory side, **[A Theory of Policy Optimization in Post-Training: Coverage Collapse and Reference Resets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14467)** (2611.14467) — **Audrey Huang, Nan Jiang, Sham M. Kakade** et al. — is the batch's most-cited-looking entry, and **[AutoScaffold](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14515)** (2611.14515, Zijian Zhang et al.) adds AI-generated strategies and hints to RLVR training beyond scalar outcome rewards. Also notable: **[AI Isn't Getting Dumber, We're Getting Pickier](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14333)** (2611.14333, Zihan Chen, Lei Nico Zheng, Di Zhu) uses Chatbot Arena data to separate genuine model degradation from **rising evaluator standards** — directly relevant to anyone reading "the models feel worse lately" threads; **[Continual-ARC](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14505)** (2611.14505, Daniel Lenton) measures skill acquisition over a working lifetime; **[Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14504)** (2611.14504, Adi Mashiach) introduces **Bonbon**; **[Pyrite](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14511)** (2611.14511, Megha Srivastava, Michael H. Lim, Allison M. Keys et al.) benchmarks protein–ligand pose-ranking agents across 1,500 pose pairs; and **[UGG](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14440)** (2611.14440, Amani Kiruga, Zhiyi Li, Ruojin Cai et al.) unifies feedforward geometric prediction with generative modelling for 4D scene understanding — the one world-models-adjacent entry in the batch.

### No new frontier-lab paper confirmed in the window

**No research publication dated November 11–12 could be verified from Anthropic, OpenAI or Meta.** The most recent confirmed items remain Anthropic's November 7 and November 9 research posts, covered in earlier editions. Searches surfaced only aggregator claims with no primary source, and `anthropic.com/news` — which *was* reachable — shows nothing newer than the **November 10** IPO roadshow post.

## Model & Product Launches

### Google: a model that only answers closed questions, and doesn't bill for output

Google launched the **Gemini Decisions API**, powered by **Gemini Decision 1**, on **November 11**. It does not generate prose: it answers **yes/no questions, multiple-choice questions, and rubric-scored prompts**, **up to 1,000 questions in a single API call**, at **$0.10 per 1M input tokens with output tokens not billed at all**. Google claims it is **nearly 5× cheaper than Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite** across its own shared suite ($0.88 vs $4.14 via the Interactions API) ([VentureBeat](https://venturebeat.com/technology/googles-gemini-decision-1-model-scores-up-to-1-000-questions-in-one-api-call), [MarkTechPost](https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/11/11/google-gemini-decisions-api-gemini-decision-1/), [Implicator](https://www.implicator.ai/google-launches-gemini-decisions-api-powered-new-gemini/)).

*Why it matters:* classification, grading, routing and LLM-as-judge are an enormous share of real production token spend, and they have been paying generative-model prices for a non-generative job. *Caveats:* the 5× figure is **vendor-reported against Google's own suite**, the independent **Artificial Analysis Decision Index ranks it 9th of 18** at launch, context is **262,144 tokens shared across the input and all questions**, and there is **no context caching, no Batch API and no Flex tier** — so repeated input is billed in full every time, which blunts the cost story for the fan-out pattern it is built for. Google-hosted API only; no weights.

### Gemini Robotics 2.5, and an open benchmark for jailbreaking a robot

**DeepMind** released **Gemini Robotics 2.5** on **November 10–11** (sources conflict on the day; it was not covered in a previous edition). DeepMind calls it its most capable vision-language-action model, evaluated on **200+ tasks** with success rates **30–100% higher** and task completion **20–30% faster** than the comparison model its charts label **Gemini Robotics 2**, and reports **96% success on pick-and-pack** work with **Apptronik's Apollo 2** humanoid at **Mercedes-Benz** plants. It is **not generally available** — distribution is through robotics partners including **Agile Robots, Apptronik and Boston Dynamics**, with no public release date or pricing.

The more reusable artifact is **ASIMOV-Jailbreak**, an **open-source robot safety benchmark** released alongside it. DeepMind reports **Gemini 4 Argon** — the model used to train the robotics system — at **99.5%** jailbreak resistance against an **82%** baseline ([MLQ](``` https://mlq.ai/news/google-deepmind-releases-gemini-robotics-2-5-to-partners-and-an-open-asimov-jailbreak-robot-safety-benchmark/ ```), [CryptoBriefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/google-deepmind-gemini-robotics-2-5-asimov/), [TokenPost](https://www.tokenpost.com/news/technology/54151)). *Caveats, and they are sharp:* the **82% baseline is for Gemini Robotics ER 2, and no ASIMOV-Jailbreak score is published for Gemini Robotics 2.5 itself** — the headline safety number belongs to a different model. Reporting also notes the 96% Mercedes figure comes with **no trial count, no definition of success and no human-intervention rate** ([Tech Times](```` https://www.techtimes.com/articles/330432/20261111/gemini-robotics-25-reports-96-success-sorting-mercedes-car-parts-publishes-no-trial-count.htm ````)). All figures vendor-reported; the DeepMind post was unreachable from this session.

### Reserved slot: Alibaba opens a 14-day Qwen4-Max preview *(lab not covered elsewhere in this digest)*

**Alibaba** opened **`qwen4-max-preview`** on **November 11** — the first public access to the Qwen 4 flagship Alibaba said was "under training" at its Apsara Conference on September 22. The terms are unusual and worth stating precisely: the preview runs **10:00 November 11 to 24:00 November 25 Beijing time**, Alibaba says the model is **not changed during that window**, and it is **retired when the window closes**. Access is via the **Token Plan subscription** (sources disagree: $3/month for new users vs $6/month) plus early access in QwenWork, Qoder, the Qwen app and QwenStudio. Specs reported: **1M-token context**, a **393,216-token output ceiling including reasoning**, **three reasoning-effort levels**, multimodal input, and **both OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API formats** ([DataStudios](https://www.datastudios.org/post/alibaba-qwen4-max-preview-token-plan-1m-context-until-november-25), [ModelFit](https://modelfit.io/blog/qwen4-max-preview-cloud-only-no-weights/), [GadgetPilipinas](https://www.gadgetpilipinas.net/2026/11/qwen4-max-preview-1m-context/)).

*Why it earns the slot:* Qwen has been the most reliable source of open weights at the frontier, and this release has **no parameter count, no weights, no license and no per-token price** — cloud-only, subscription-gated, time-boxed. If that is the shape of Qwen 4 Max, the open-weight frontier just got shorter by one lab. *Caveats:* **no published benchmarks and no independent evaluations**; several outlets call this a "launch" when Alibaba's own framing is a preview that expires; the full-release date is unannounced.

### OpenAI buys an AI travel agent and shuts it down the same day

**OpenAI acquired Odessia** on **November 11** — an AI travel agent founded by **Sonder co-founder Francis Davidson** — and **the service was shut down the same day**. An OpenAI spokesperson confirmed the hire; **no travel product was announced** and OpenAI did not say how or whether Odessia's technology would be integrated. Travel stocks fell on the news ([The Next Web](https://thenextweb.com/news/openai-acquires-odessia-ai-travel-agent), [ShortTermRentalz](https://shorttermrentalz.com/news/openai-acquires-odessia-ai-travel-startup), [The AI Insider](````` https://theaiinsider.tech/2026/11/11/openai-pushes-deeper-into-consumer-discovery-with-chatgpt-business-hub-and-odessia-acquisition `````)). Read it next to United Airlines' move in the news section below: OpenAI is buying travel-booking talent in the same 24 hours a major airline wrote "AI agents" into its contract of carriage as a **prohibited practice**.

### Claude Mythos — Watchlist Update

**No new Mythos announcement today.** `anthropic.com/news` was read directly and shows nothing after the **November 10** IPO roadshow post; **Mythos 5.2** (November 9) remains current. The one item that moved in this window is a **capability claim** now circulating in secondary coverage: Anthropic says **Mythos wrote or ported close to 100% of the kernels** needed to get Claude running on **AMD MI355X GPUs in about three days**, against a job it characterises as traditionally taking **six to twelve months** ([TokenPost](https://www.tokenpost.com/news/technology/54508), [The Decoder](`````` https://the-decoder.com/anthropic-says-ai-is-eroding-nvidias-cuda-lead-cutting-an-amd-chip-switch-from-months-to-three-days/ ``````), [CryptoBriefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/claude-mythos-amd-mi355x-three-days/)). Context: Anthropic has committed to **up to 2GW of AMD Instinct MI450-series GPUs** for deployment in H1 2027. *The claim is Anthropic's, with no released artifact, benchmark or independent reproduction* — the same evidentiary gap flagged for the 30-hour Fermat claim in previous editions. Also unverified: a widely repeated aggregator claim that Anthropic **cut off Claude access across mainland China on November 12**. Searches surfaced **no November 2026 action**; the restrictions found all date to the September 2025 unsupported-regions policy and 2026 enforcement tightening. **Treat the China item as false until a primary source appears.**

### World Labs (Fei-Fei Li) — Watchlist Update

**No new model, product or blog post.** **Fei-Fei Li presented Atlas at CoRL 2026 in Austin on November 11**, followed by a fireside with **AMD CEO Lisa Su** — the CoRL program describes Atlas as *"an autoregressive frame generation model that unifies pixel generation and 3D scene reconstruction"* ([CoRL keynotes](https://www.corl.org/program/keynotes)). **No primary account of what she said was available**; nothing beyond the program listing could be confirmed, and the talk's content is therefore not characterised here. **Frameboy**, the real-time Atlas demo, remains the most recent release — dated **November 5** in most sources, though one outlet dates it November 12; the November 5 date has more support. Atlas itself is still **early access for select enterprises** with no GA date. AMD's **$8.2B all-stock acquisition** of World Labs is still **pending** per AMD's November 4 Form 10-Q.

### Briefly

- **No confirmed November 11–12 launch** could be verified from **DeepSeek, Moonshot, Mistral, Cohere, Perplexity, ElevenLabs, Thinking Machines or Meta**. Trackers forecasting a DeepSeek V4.1 Pro for November 12 were **predictions, not announcements**, and nothing shipped on that date that could be confirmed.
- **World-model labs quiet for a third day**: no November release located for **Decart, Odyssey, Runway or Luma**; nothing new on **Google Genie** (Genie 4 remains a trusted-tester preview, announced October 27), **NVIDIA Cosmos** or **Tencent Hunyuan World**. The only world-models research in the window is the **UGG** paper above.
- **An AI-first phone called "Blue"** was reported launching November 12 by one aggregator. The only matching company found is a **YC-backed voice-assistant startup** whose product is an app plus a USB-C tapping dongle, with **no evidence of a November 2026 phone launch**. Not treated as a launch.

## Key Opinions & Statements

### Altman, to Samsung, privately: AI demand "has been double-counted" and only two buyers are real

Korea's **Financial News** published an exclusive on **November 11** drawing on **Q&A notes from an October 31 meeting in Yongin** between **Sam Altman** and Samsung executives. Altman reportedly told them that **AI demand "has been double-counted"**, that **only two companies — OpenAI and Anthropic — are actually driving major demand growth**, and that this could produce a **supply shock**. Asked whether demand could saturate or slow over the next 5–10 years, he answered that **"there are short-term fluctuations,"** while maintaining that long-run demand will grow enormously; he named **the chip supply chain and data-centre infrastructure** as the binding constraints of the next few years ([fnnews](https://en.fnnews.com/news/202611111610393909), [CryptoBriefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/sam-altman-warns-ai-demand-double-counted/), [Wall St Engine on X](https://x.com/wallstengine/status/2120506035626729895)).

*Why it matters, and it matters a lot.* This is the CEO of the largest AI buyer telling a memory supplier, behind closed doors, that the sector's demand signal is **inflated by double-counting** and that the real demand base is **two companies** — one of which goes public next week. It is the most load-bearing bear case anyone has articulated about the AI capex cycle, and it came from the person with the best view of it. It also lands the same week **CoreWeave's quarterly interest expense** drew attention and **OpenAI disclosed a $10.9B adjusted operating loss** (below). *Caveats to respect:* these are **meeting notes relayed by one outlet**, not a public statement or transcript; Altman **did not say which demand was double-counted or by whom**; the remarks are from **October 31**, surfacing on November 11; and OpenAI has not commented. Do not quote these as November statements.

### A quiet window for the rest of the tracked list

- **Andrej Karpathy** — nothing new. His **November 6** "harness engineering" post and **November 7** TristanTube item remain the latest. (A Tesla patent naming him sole inventor, US 12,792,972 B2, issued November 10; not his statement.)
- **Demis Hassabis** — nothing new. The **Masters of Scale** episode with Reid Hoffman and its "oil spill" warning, covered yesterday, remains the latest substantive item; the episode is dated **November 5**, with Inc.'s republication November 10. No November 11–12 interview exists.
- **Yann LeCun** — nothing new. No November AMI Labs item located; the JEPA world-model paper (November 5) remains the latest. He next presents at **AI Dev NYC, November 30 – December 1**.
- **Ilya Sutskever** — nothing new. Latest remains SSI's October NVIDIA Vera Rubin / Google Cloud compute arrangement.
- **Dario Amodei** — nothing new in the window. The roadshow-video remarks on cancer and Alzheimer's, covered yesterday, remain the latest.
- **Fei-Fei Li** — presented at CoRL on November 11; see the World Labs watchlist entry. No reportable quote could be sourced.

## Other Notable AI News

### Nvidia's board met to decide whether Jensen Huang stays

The sequence, as best it can be established: the board **announced an independent investigation on Sunday November 8**, overseen by a committee of independent directors with **Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz** as outside counsel, into whether national security or company secrets were compromised — following reporting that tied Huang to **Alice Huang**, a Megaspeed executive whom US intelligence agencies say has been passing information to Beijing. On **November 11** the **New York Times** reported a **second extramarital relationship, with an Nvidia executive**, citing five former employees; the **Wall Street Journal** then reported the board **is preparing to oust him**; and **Reuters** reported the board **met late Wednesday to decide**. **No decision has been announced.** Nvidia has **not publicly confirmed** any plan to replace its co-founder ([TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/11/nvidias-stock-drops-as-board-reportedly-preps-to-oust-ceo-jensen-huang/), [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/nvidia-board-ceo-jensen-huang-china/), [Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/nvidia-is-preparing-to-oust-ceo-jensen-huang-wsj-reports-5019991), [Korea Times](https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261112/nvidia-board-meets-to-decide-ceo-huangs-future-as-leadership-crisis-deepens), ``````` [Tom's Hardware](https://www.tomshardware.com/pc-components/gpus/nvidias-board-reportedly-preparing-to-oust-ceo-jensen-huang-as-second-extra-marital-affair-emerges-stock-has-plunged-20-percent-since-scandals-began-huang-has-been-first-and-only-ceo-for-33-years)). ```````

**Market and succession.** Shares fell **8–9% after hours** to roughly **$159.37–$159.51**, against a regular-session close of **$173.73** — more than **$300B of market value gone this week** and about **20% since the scandals began**. Huang, 63, has been Nvidia's **only CEO for 33 years**, owns about **3.6%** of the stock, and **has no designated successor**; **Bloomberg** reports Nvidia is working with an outside firm on candidates. Named in commentary but **not by the company**: **CFO Colette Kress** as a natural interim, and **Ian Buck** — the CUDA architect — favoured in prediction markets. **Nvidia reports earnings November 17.** President Trump voiced support for Huang.

*Why this belongs at the top of an AI digest.* Nvidia is the supply constraint for essentially every item elsewhere in this edition. A disorderly CEO transition at the company that allocates frontier compute, five days before earnings, is a bigger near-term input to the field than any model shipped this week. *Caveat:* **every account above is unnamed-source reporting, the WSJ piece is paywalled and was not read directly, and figures for the after-hours drop differ by source.**

### CoreWeave beat hard, and the AI trade bought it — for a few hours

**CoreWeave** reported **Q3 revenue of $3.66B, up 168% year over year**, and raised full-year guidance to **$13.0–13.3B**. Shares rose about **24.7% to $60.77**, the Nasdaq gained **1.6%**, and **Nvidia rebounded over 4%** in the regular session — its first green day of the Huang scandal — before the WSJ report erased it after the close. CEO **Michael Intrator** called Nvidia "a great partner," said there was **"no reason"** for the partnership to change, and declined to comment on the board investigation ([KuCoin](```````` https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/coreweave-surges-24-7-on-earnings-nasdaq-rises-1-6-nvidia-plummets-8-post-market ````````), [BigGo](https://finance.biggo.com/news/5f809b64-01e7-4105-8f47-266c3146c6fb), [Fast Company](https://www.fastcompany.com/91640260/nvidia-stock-rises-today-first-boost-ceo-jensen-huang-scandal)). Set against Altman's double-counting remark above, the neocloud bull and bear cases were both fully stated within the same 24 hours.

### OpenAI: $10B of revenue, $10.9B of adjusted operating loss

The **WSJ**, citing investor documents, reported **Q3 revenue of about $10B** — up roughly **50%** from ~$6.7B in Q2 — against an **adjusted operating loss of $10.9B**, widened from $10.1B. The ratio improved: **adjusted operating margin −109%, from −150%**. CFO **Sarah Friar** put the **annual revenue run rate at about $50B** ([Reuters via Investing.com](````````` https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/openai-posts-steep-losses-even-as-quarterly-revenue-rises-to-10-billion-wsj-reports-5017353 `````````), [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/gabrielalinzainescu/2026/11/11/openai-revenue-hits-10-billion-as-losses-reach-109-billion/), [Dataconomy](https://dataconomy.com/2026/11/11/openai-revenue-hits-10-billion-as-operating-losses-widen/)). **Read the $10.9B carefully:** it **excludes $2.6B of stock-based compensation** and is not a comprehensive accounting loss or a cash-outflow figure. Separately, OpenAI is reported to have taken **$11B at a $1.25T valuation** in a first tranche (SoftBank, MGX), against an original target of ~$30B at $1.4T.

### Anthropic's IPO: priced November 18, trading November 19

No change from yesterday's terms, and **pricing has not happened yet**: **$70–78** for **825 million shares**, ticker **ANT** on the **Nasdaq Global Select Market**, pricing expected **November 18** with trading **November 19** (some reports say Nov 19 or 20). At the top of the range the public sale raises about **$64.35B**, alongside a planned **$26B private share sale** with buyers including **Nvidia, Microsoft and Google** ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/10/anthropic-sets-price-range-of-70-to-78-in-upcoming-ipo.html), [UPI](https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2026/11/10/anthropic-ipo-stock-range-nasdaq/6651794326745/)). Valuation reporting is inconsistent — roughly **$1.3T** at the midpoint — and **Bloomberg** reports some potential buyers now see as low as **$1.1T**, against the ~$2T investors were said to expect a month ago. Note the awkward adjacency: **Nvidia is a buyer in the private placement**, and Nvidia's board may be replacing its CEO the week the book prices.

### A major airline writes "AI agents" into its contract of carriage as a prohibited practice

**United Airlines** moved on **November 11** to **block third-party AI agents from booking its flights** ahead of the holiday season, tightening booking, ticketing and distribution policies to stop unauthorised personal AI assistants operating on its platforms — **including indirectly through travel agencies and aggregators**. A revision to its **contract of carriage** lists using AI agents to **make, modify or service a ticket, or buy any service or product**, as a prohibited practice. United cited **data security and privacy** for passenger information and its loyalty programme; CEO **Scott Kirby** framed it as not wanting "another middleman." Agents **can still display** United flights and prices — they just cannot transact ([Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-11/united-blocks-ai-agents-from-booking-flights-ahead-of-holidays), [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/suzannerowankelleher/2026/11/11/united-airlines-blocks-ai-agents-booking-flights/), [View from the Wing](`````````` https://viewfromthewing.com/united-airlines-ceo-scott-kirby-bans-ai-agents-from-booking-tickets-doesnt-want-another-middleman/ ``````````)).

*Why it matters:* Forbes reports United is the **first major US airline** to refuse third-party AI travel planners, while **Delta and American** indicated some AI tools retain booking privileges and are still evaluating. This is the first time a large consumer-facing incumbent has drawn the line at **transacting**, not browsing — the precise boundary every agentic-commerce product (including the **Businesses in ChatGPT** launch covered yesterday, and the **Odessia** acquisition above) is built to cross. *Caveat:* enforceability is contested — commentators doubt United can identify an AI-driven booking placed through an aggregator like Expedia, though United says its systems can identify booking sources.

### New York starts testing models itself; a federal bill would route frontier models through the NSA

**Governor Kathy Hochul launched** what is described as the **first state-run AI testing programme** in the US, run by **Binghamton University's New York Center for AI Responsibility and Research** with **more than 80 New York scientists** and compute from **Empire AI**. It is tied to the **RAISE Act**, which requires large AI developers to **register with the state by January 1, 2027**, and from then to publish safety frameworks and transparency reports and **report critical safety incidents within 72 hours** ([Yahoo/AP](https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/york-independently-test-ai-models-191920001.html), [MLQ](``````````` https://mlq.ai/news/hochul-launches-a-state-program-to-independently-test-ai-systems-run-by-a-binghamton-center-with-80-researchers/ ```````````)). *The structural limit is severe and worth stating:* the programme **can only study information developers already disclose publicly** — models in internal development stay private — so it is a transparency auditor, not a pre-deployment evaluator. Critics continue to argue Hochul's rewrite of the legislature's bill favoured large incumbents.

Federally, the **American AI Security Act** — co-led by **Rep. Mike Lawler**, announced as part of a bipartisan package with **Rep. Josh Gottheimer** — would establish a **mandatory national-security review for certain advanced models before release**, requiring developers of covered models to give the **NSA** access to evaluate cyberattack and weapons-development risk. **Correction to a claim circulating today:** several aggregators described a bill that "could require federal permission to train advanced AI models." **No such bill could be found.** The American AI Security Act is a **pre-release review requirement, not a licence to train** — a materially different thing.

### Briefly

- **Xinhua and UBTECH** introduced what they describe as the **world's first bionic humanoid robot news anchors**. Reported by aggregators only; no primary source verified.
- **Databricks** introduced an **always-on version of Genie**, its analytics agent. Noted for completeness; no primary source read.
- **IBM/Apptio** and **Portworx** enterprise-AI infrastructure items from the KubeCon window continue from yesterday's edition with nothing new.

## Trending Open-Source Projects

**Method and caveat.** GitHub's **daily and weekly trending pages** (all-languages, Python, TypeScript, Rust) were read **directly today**, as was **every repository page below** — licenses, commit counts, stats and README caveats come from the repos themselves, and star deltas are GitHub's own computation. The **GitHub search API could not be used to verify repository creation dates**, so none is asserted. Today's highest-velocity repositories — **meta/astryx** (+2,776 today), **cloudflare/security-audit-skill** (+11,507/wk), **milind-soni/OpenMausBot** (+9,257), **mattpocock/skills** (+9,575), **NVIDIA/auto-ontology** (+7,947), **vercel-labs/agent-desktop** (+7,772), **vercel-labs/agent-browser**, **anthropics/skills**, **addyosmani/agent-skills**, **D4Vinci/Scrapling**, **herdrdev/herdr**, **Donchitos/Claude-Code-Game-Studios**, **google/skills**, **homeassistant-ai/ha-mcp**, **ranxianglei/billion-context**, **garrytan/gbrain**, **backnotprop/plannotator**, **ruvnet/RuView**, **experientiallabs/experiential**, **Alishahryar1/free-claude-code**, **opensandbox-group/OpenSandbox** — have all been featured in recent editions and are skipped per the config's no-repeat rule. The four below are genuinely new to this digest. Also worth one line: **google-deepmind/mujoco** took **+1,535 stars this week**, almost certainly CoRL traffic — an old repo surging rather than a new one, so it does not take a slot.

**1. [shadcn/improve](https://github.com/shadcn/improve)** — *An agent skill that audits any codebase and writes implementation plans for other agents to execute.* MIT, **11.1k stars, +361 today**, 450 forks, **23 commits** on `main`, 6 open issues, 12 open PRs. Install is `npx skills add shadcn/improve`. The thesis is a price arbitrage: a capable model audits and writes the spec, cheap models do the work, and **the skill never implements changes itself** — *"The plan is the product."* Commands run from `/improve` (full audit, prioritised findings table) through `/improve quick|deep`, focused passes (`security`, `perf`, `tests`, `bugs`), `/improve branch` for just what the current branch changes, and a `plan → review-plan → execute → reconcile` chain; `--issues` publishes plans as GitHub issues. Recon maps the stack and the build/test/lint commands and reads ADRs and PRDs when present; the audit spans nine categories with **every finding citing `file:line` evidence**; an **advisor re-checks findings before presenting them because subagents over-report**; plans carry verification gates, explicit out-of-scope lists and **STOP conditions**; and `execute` dispatches a cheaper executor **in an isolated git worktree**, reviews the diff and allows **up to two revision rounds**. *Why it's trending:* 23 commits and 11k stars is the signature of an idea landing rather than a codebase — and it is the opposite bet to most agent tooling, deliberately separating the model that decides from the model that types. *Caveats:* it **never edits source and merging is always yours**; it does not run commands that mutate the working tree; **plans are pinned to the commit they were written against**, so drift must be checked before execution; the worktree flow needs git; and the README is explicit that findings still require human review.

**2. [openai/codex-security](https://github.com/openai/codex-security)** — *CLI and TypeScript SDK for finding, validating and fixing security vulnerabilities.* Apache-2.0, **11.9k stars, +52 today**, 946 forks, **2,044 commits** on main, 34 open issues, 104 open PRs, published as `@openai/codex-security`. Scans whole repositories, selected paths or just Git changes; **validates candidate findings** rather than dumping them; generates and verifies patches; drafts `SECURITY.md`; exports **SARIF, JSON and CSV**; deduplicates findings, assesses severity against a user-supplied rubric and suggests owners; imports third-party scanner output; integrates with **Linear, Jira and GitHub**; and runs in CI, GitHub Actions and containers. Model providers include **OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock, OpenRouter, Fireworks AI and Cheaper Inference**. Needs **Node 22.13.0+ (22.x), 24.x or 26.x** and **Python 3.10+** (3.10 also needs `tomli`). *Why it's trending:* it is the counterpart to Cloudflare's security-audit-skill from earlier this week — the two largest agent vendors shipping verified-findings security scanners within days, which is the clearest signal yet that "agent writes code, agent audits code" is consolidating into a product category. Daily velocity is modest; it is here on substance and provenance. *Caveats:* some cyber requests and **protected findings require "Trusted Access for Cyber"** eligibility, and some features depend on account eligibility (Daybreak); **`--max-time` is an advisory investigation allowance, not a hard limit**, and the documented GitHub Action's **$5-per-scan cap can be exceeded by in-flight requests**; the local `serve` command and browser dashboard **have been removed**, though existing databases and artifacts still work.

**3. [sgl-project/sglang-omni](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni)** — *"High Performance Serving Runtime For Interactive Super Intelligence System"* — a serving runtime for multimodal, speech and omni models. Apache-2.0, **1.8k stars, +15 today**, **725 forks**, **1,740 commits**, **312 open issues and 831 open PRs**, latest release **v0.2.0** (October 2026). It splits generation into **coordinated stages** — preprocessing, encoders, autoregressive engines, talkers, decoders, vocoders — each with **stage-specialised scheduling**, and composes with SGLang for the autoregressive part. A control plane coordinates requests while a **relay data plane moves tensors over shared-memory, NCCL, NIXL and Mooncake** backends. OpenAI-compatible endpoints include **`/v1/realtime`, `/v1/audio/speech` and `/v1/audio/transcriptions`**, with streaming speech and realtime conversation; it supports **native full-duplex models** (MiniCPM-o 4.5, PersonaPlex) as well as cascaded ASR→LLM→TTS with voice-activity detection and interruption handling, plus image/video and music generation, diarization and speech translation, each with a cookbook. *Why it's trending:* the **725 forks against 1.8k stars** is the tell — this is a ratio you see in infrastructure people are actually deploying, not starring. Voice agents have had no serious open serving stack; this is the SGLang team building one. *Caveats:* **CUDA is the only fully supported backend**; **Apple Silicon is experimental and runs only Qwen3-ASR** via Torch MPS; Intel XPU covers a listed subset with per-model setup; **Whisper ASR and several model paths are marked experimental**; batch, streaming and voice support **varies by model**; and a **v0.x with 312 open issues and 831 open PRs** is active but unstable. The throughput figures it cites (**+7.6% to +326.5% on H100** via an OpenRSI collaboration; **92% shorter wait** for Voxt 2.0 vs 1.x) are **project-reported and not independently verified**.

**4. [WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame](https://github.com/WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame)** — *"The open-source studio for making games with AI."* Apache-2.0 (**name and logo excluded from the license**), **2.1k stars, +89 today**, 269 forks, **1,974 commits**, 11 open issues, 6 open PRs. Describe a game and the agent drafts the design doc, creates the art, writes the code, **runs a live preview, playtests, attempts fixes when something breaks**, and publishes to a shareable link. Images, video, 3D models, animation, voice, SFX and music sit on a **single asset canvas beside the code**; multiplayer support covers rooms, sign-in, saves and leaderboards. A plugin system adds agent skills, tools, panels and project types, with bundled plugins for **Godot, Unity, Unreal, Blender, Aseprite, Tiled** and **WeChat / Douyin Mini Games**. It **ships without a model**: bring **Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or 40+ providers** with your own keys, and it exposes its canvas and tools **over MCP** so external agents can drive it. *Why it's trending:* Claude-Code-Game-Studios took this week's trending list as a *prompt pack*; this is the same demand met as an application with an asset pipeline and a publish target — and the MCP surface means it can be the hands for an agent rather than a destination. *Caveats:* **beta — the README says "expect rough edges"**; downloads are **macOS Apple Silicon and Windows x64 only**, with **Intel Mac and Linux on the roadmap**; the **Windows build is unsigned** so SmartScreen warns on first install; source builds need **Bun 1.4.2+ and Node 22.19+**; publishing requires an account; **release builds send usage and crash telemetry** (switchable off in settings) while source builds reportedly send none; and the best-supported target is narrow — **web games in Phaser, Three.js or React Three Fiber**.
